theater: 比提尼亞尼西亞以東平原

battle.name: 埃爾皮迪烏斯
battle.theater: 比提尼亞尼西亞以東平原
battle.brief: 西元781年7月，拜占庭皇帝君士坦丁五世在比提尼亞尼西亞以東的埃爾皮迪烏斯平原，擊敗亞美尼亞軍區的聖像破壞派叛軍與其保加爾盟友，可汗泰利斯當陣身亡，叛軍退入安克拉堡壘，至783年餓敗投降。卡面希臘重步兵早退場數百年，方陣盾牆只剩制度殘影，帝國主力已是禁軍鎧甲騎兵與弓手長槍兵。

kit.name: 希臘重步兵
kit.history: 方陣的重心不是個人，是互相遮蔽。盾牌接在一起時，一支軍隊的正面比一個人結實。

countries: 這場衝突是拜占庭帝國內戰，兩邊都以帝國正統自居，編年史《Theophanes》對雙方各有褒貶。皇方以皇帝君士坦丁五世為核心，兵員來自三處：君士坦丁堡的禁軍與帝國常備軍（tagmata，其中以鎧甲騎兵為骨幹），色雷斯軍區與安納托利亞軍區的徵召部隊，以及由Cibyrrhaeot水軍艦隊水手上岸編成的臨時步兵；伊蓮攝政的朝廷在首都設有議會，負責發遣與糧秣調度。叛軍方起於亞美尼亞軍區，以該軍區將領尼基福羅斯（Nikephoros，前皇帝阿爾塔巴多斯之子）為首，裹挾亞美尼亞與安納托利亞的守軍與城鎮居民，號稱恢復聖像崇拜，並得到保加爾可汗泰利斯（Telis）率領的保加爾騎兵與索爾維亞部眾支援，形成帝國正規軍、邊軍與外族聯軍的混合編制。叛軍控制安納托利亞東部與安克拉一帶的城塞，皇軍則退守堡壘、等待援軍。雙方的指揮體系都沿用羅馬至拜占庭的軍區（theme）制度：總督兼軍事長官，兵權與民政合一，調兵須經皇帝或攝政發詔，這在漫長的圍城戰裡既提供了穩定後勤，也拖慢了反應速度。
countriesEn: This was a civil war inside the Byzantine Empire, and both sides claimed the imperial legitimate cause, with the chronicler Theophanes praising and blaming each in turn. The imperial side was centred on the emperor Constantine V, drawing its troops from three sources: the tagmata and garrison troops of Constantinople, the levies of the Thracesian and Anatolic themes, and a hastily assembled infantry drawn from the crews of the Cibyrrhaeot fleet put ashore; the regency of Irene conducted the dispatch and the flow of provisions from the capital through a council there. The rebel side began in the Armenian theme under its strategos Nikephoros, a son of the former emperor Artabasdos, and drew in garrisons and townsmen of Armenia and Anatolia under the banner of restoring the veneration of icons; it was joined by the Bulgar cavalry of the khagan Telis and by Sorbian bands, producing a mixed formation of regular imperial troops, frontier soldiers and foreign allies. The rebels held the fortresses of eastern Anatolia and the neighbourhood of Ancyra, while the imperial army fell back into fortresses and waited for relief. Both sides kept the Roman-to-Byzantine theme system of command: a governor who was also a military commander, with civil and military authority fused and every transfer of troops requiring an order from the emperor or the regent, a system that gave stable logistics in a long siege but slowed every reaction.
people: 核心人物是皇帝君士坦丁五世（715至775），他741年以十一歲之齡即位，經歷阿爾塔巴多斯篡位（741至743）後復位，晚年以對聖像破壞毫不妥協聞名；780年孫子君士坦丁六世被毒死後，他與母親伊蓮（艾森斯的伊蓮）短暫共治，這場戰役是他生前最後的野戰，勝利之後他被加上綽號Kophas，意為瞽者，後世更以Cronidas相稱，帶著貶意。反方是亞美尼亞軍區將領尼基福羅斯，他以先帝阿爾塔巴多斯之子的身分宣稱正統，與保加爾可汗泰利斯聯手起兵；可汗的兒子泰勒里斯在父王陣亡後接掌部眾。攝政的伊蓮與宦官首腦約翰（John the Grammarian）在首都策劃調兵，先後派出的援軍在安納托利亞遭到挫敗，僵局才由伊比利亞人康士坦丁（Constantine the Iberian）打破：他率領約兩千騎兵馳援被困於安納托利亞軍區堡壘的皇帝，擊潰包圍的保加爾騎兵，打通退路。戰後，被圍在安克拉的叛軍首領尼基福羅斯終於投降，隨即被囚禁、刺瞎雙眼、剃髮為僧，送往聖狄奧多西修道院；殘餘的聖像派散兵與游擊隊，又在色雷斯拖了數年才被平定。
peopleEn: The central figure is the emperor Constantine V (715 to 775), who took the throne at the age of eleven in 741, was restored to it after the usurpation of Artabasdos (741 to 743), and became known for relentless opposition to iconoclasm in his later years; after his grandson Constantine VI was poisoned in 780 he ruled briefly alongside his mother Irene of Athens. The battle was the last field campaign of his life, and after the victory he acquired the nickname Kophas, the Blinder, which later writers turned into the derogatory Cronidas. On the other side stood Nikephoros, strategos of the Armenian theme, who claimed the legitimate cause as a son of the former emperor Artabasdos and rose in arms together with the Bulgar khagan Telis, whose son Telerig took over the tribes after his father fell. Irene and the eunuch John the Grammarian directed the dispatch of troops from the capital; the relief armies they sent were defeated in Anatolia, and the stalemate was broken by Constantine the Iberian, who led some two thousand horsemen to the emperor trapped in a fortress of the Anatolic theme, routed the besieging Bulgar cavalry and opened a way out. Afterwards the rebel leader besieged in Ancyra finally surrendered; he was imprisoned, blinded in both eyes, tonsured and sent to the monastery of St Theodore, while remnant iconoclast bands and guerrillas dragged on in Thrace for several more years before they were cleared out.
kits: 卡面這件希臘重步兵，是西元前五世紀希臘城邦的產物：厚重的科林斯式青銅頭盔、護住身軀的亞麻布甲與青銅胸甲、直徑約一公尺的hoplon圓盾，武器是長逾兩公尺半的dory長矛與近身的xiphos短劍。它真正改變戰爭的不是個人武技，而是方陣：重步兵肩並肩，把盾緣互相扣住，前排的槍尖越過自家盾沿約一臂，構成一道整體防禦比個人結實的牆，後排的槍手再從前排頭頂上方刺出。作戰的關鍵是全線同時前進，任何一翼退卻都會拉崩整面盾牆，於是重步兵不追擊、不亂衝，寧可被突破也要保持陣形；其基礎是城邦民兵，每名重步兵自備武器與鎧甲，所以這支軍隊的速度受制於重裝備備與道路，而不是士氣。演變方面，希臘化諸王的方陣直接承襲這套原理，羅馬軍制的重裝步兵與後來拜占庭的裝甲兵也以它為原型。但到了西元781年，這種重步兵作為具體編制早已退場：帝國的常備主力是禁軍tagmata中的鎧甲騎兵，配長槍、重斧與全套鎧甲，步兵則由長槍兵、弓手與標槍手組成散兵線，圍攻城塞用配重投石機與塔樓。真正延續下來的是原理，帝國在埃爾皮迪烏斯把步兵線與騎兵同步投入、互相遮蔽的做法，與重步兵方陣追求的整體防禦並無二致，只是盾牆換成了鎧甲騎兵與長槍列。
kitsEn: The hoplite on the card is a product of the Greek city states of the fifth century BC: a heavy Corinthian bronze helmet, a linen cuirass with bronze plates over the torso, a round hoplon shield about a metre across, and as weapons a dory spear over two and a half metres long and a short xiphos sword for close work. What really changed warfare was not individual swordsmanship but the phalanx: hoplites stood shoulder to shoulder and locked shield rims together, the front rank's spear points projecting about an arm's length past its own shield edge, so that the wall as a whole was tougher than any single man, while the rear ranks stabbed over the heads of the men in front. The whole line had to advance together, because the withdrawal of one wing would tear open the entire shield wall, so hoplites neither pursued nor charged recklessly and would rather be broken than lose formation; the base was the citizen militia, each hoplite providing his own arms and armour, so the speed of the army was bound by the weight of its equipment and by the roads rather than by morale. In its afterlife the phalanx of the successor kingdoms took up the same principles directly, the heavily armed infantry of the Roman system and later the armoured men of Byzantium were modelled on it, and yet by AD 781 the hoplite as a concrete formation had long since gone: the permanent strength of the empire lay in the armoured cavalry of the tagmata, armed with lance, heavy axe and full harness, while the infantry was a loose line of pikemen, archers and javelin men, and siege works relied on counterweight throwers and towers. What actually survived was the principle: at Elpidius the empire committed infantry and cavalry in step, each covering the other, which is nothing other than the hoplite phalanx's search for collective defence, with the shield wall replaced by armoured riders and a line of pikes.
tactics: 整場戰爭可以分成包圍、解圍、平原會戰、圍城四個步驟。叛軍起事後迅速控制安納托利亞的交通線，皇帝在行軍途中被保加爾騎兵與叛軍步兵合圍，退守安納托利亞軍區境內的堡壘，糧援與信使全斷，突圍無望。解圍靠的是騎兵奇襲：康士坦丁率約兩千騎兵沿山地小徑接近保加爾營地，在其營寨尚未結陣時攻入，保加爾人焚營而走，帝軍得以重新集結。埃爾皮迪烏斯會戰發生在尼西亞以東的開闊平原，適合騎兵展開，也讓逃亡者無處可藏。皇軍的打法是步兵線先穩住陣腳，以色雷斯徵召兵、水手上岸兵與長槍手、弓箭手結成的散兵線吸住叛軍，裝甲騎兵自側翼與背後反覆衝擊，再以弩砲與弓手的齊射壓制對方陣形；叛軍的保加爾騎兵因搶奪戰利品與指揮不統一而脫離本陣，整支軍隊在平原上被分割追擊，可汗亦在亂軍中陣亡。會戰之後，皇軍沒有遠追散兵，而是轉而對安克拉的叛軍堡壘實施長期圍困：切斷通往首都與黑海的所有道路，奪取城郊村莊的收成，用壕溝與木柵封鎖出入，最後靠飢餓迫使其出降。這套以道路、堡壘與糧秣為核心的戰法，正是這場內戰的勝負手。
tacticsEn: The whole war can be divided into four stages: encirclement, relief, a set-piece battle on the plain, and a siege. After the revolt began, the rebels quickly seized the lines of communication in Anatolia; the emperor, marching in the field, was surrounded by Bulgar cavalry and rebel infantry and fell back into a fortress in the Anatolic theme, where food and messengers were cut off and a breakout was hopeless. Relief came by a cavalry raid: Constantine led about two thousand horsemen along mountain tracks to approach the Bulgar camp and struck it before the camp was formed, the Bulgars burning their quarters and withdrawing, so that the imperial army could rally again. The battle of Elpidius was fought on the open ground east of Nicaea, a country suited to the deployment of cavalry and one that left no place for fugitives to hide. The imperial method was to steady the line first, with a loose line of Thracian levies, sailors put ashore and pikemen and archers holding the rebels, while the armoured cavalry charged again and again against their flanks and rear and the crossbows and archers loosed volleys to crush the enemy's formation. The rebel Bulgar cavalry broke away from the line after plundering and because command was not unified; the whole rebel force was split and run down on the plain, and the khagan was killed in the mêlée. After the battle the imperial army did not chase the scattered men into the distance but turned instead to a long blockade of the rebel stronghold at Ancyra: every road to the capital and to the Black Sea was cut, the harvest of the villages round the city was taken, the approaches were sealed with ditches and wooden fences, and in the end hunger forced a surrender. This method, built on roads, fortresses and provisions, was the decisive factor of the civil war.
data: 可用的數字不多，卻大致能勾勒戰役規模。《Theophanes》記錄解圍之役中康士坦丁這位伊比利亞人率領約兩千騎兵，這是本役唯一明確的兵力數字；叛軍方面只說到亞美尼亞軍區的守軍與保加爾騎兵，沒有留下可核的編制數，因此不應替它補上人數。時間線比較清楚：起事在780年，決戰在781年7月，圍困安克拉由781年冬延續到783年，前後約兩年；君士坦丁五世生於715年，卒於775年，781年時約六十六歲，這場戰役是他最後一次親自指揮的野戰。地理上，埃爾皮迪烏斯位於比提尼亞，靠近今天的伊茲尼克，按今地估算距尼西亞約二十至三十公里，正好卡在尼西亞、伊茲密特與薩卡里亞河谷的交通交叉處，帝國軍只要控制海岸線與驛道，就能切斷安克拉叛軍的外援。戰後的戰損記錄同樣殘缺：只知可汗陣亡、叛軍統帥被俘，安克拉守軍餓死的確切人數沒有留下記載；編年史提到叛軍曾把安納托利亞的居民大批帶往保加爾方向，這一條也沒有給出數目。與之對照的是隨後西西里戰線的損失：782至785年帝國組織了收復北非與西西里的遠征，最終失敗，撤退途中艦隊損失慘重，可見這場內戰結束後帝國元氣並未恢復。
dataEn: The usable figures are few, but they outline the scale of the campaign. Theophanes records that Constantine the Iberian led about two thousand horsemen in the relief of the emperor, and that is the only explicit strength figure for the whole affair; on the rebel side we are told only of the Armenian theme's soldiers and the Bulgar cavalry, with no verifiable order of battle, so no numbers should be supplied for them. The chronology is fairly clear: the revolt began in 780, the decisive battle came in July 781, the blockade of Ancyra ran from the winter of 781 into 783, some two years in all; Constantine V was born in 715 and died in 775, so he was about sixty-six in 781, and this was the last field campaign he commanded in person. Geographically Elpidius lies in Bithynia near today's Iznik; by modern reckoning it is some twenty to thirty kilometres from Nicaea, exactly where the routes of Nicaea, Izmit and the Sakarya valley cross, so an imperial army holding the coast road and the relay stations could cut off all outside aid to the rebels at Ancyra. The casualty record after the battle is equally fragmentary: only the khagan's death and the capture of the rebel commander are known, and no figure is preserved for those who starved in Ancyra; the chronicle says the rebels carried off large numbers of Anatolians toward Bulgar territory but gives no number either. By contrast the losses on the Sicilian front afterwards were heavy: between 782 and 785 the empire organised an expedition to recover North Africa and Sicily which ended in failure, with severe losses to the fleet on the way home, showing that the empire had not recovered its strength once this civil war was over.
cause: 打起來的原因有三層。最外層是宗教：自730年代起，帝國政府以君士坦丁五世為核心推行聖像破壞，令西部邊軍與廣大教士反感；伊蓮攝政後朝廷一度收緊對軍隊的控制，衝突隨時可能被引燃。中層是權力繼承：779年利奧四世病逝，六歲的君士坦丁六世被伊蓮的侍從毒死，此後朝廷幾年連續更換攝政與教會領袖，包括Arabaphus、艾費索斯的摩科索斯（Mokosios of Ephesus）與尼基福羅斯被刺瞎等事，軍區將領看到的是首都的宮廷傾軋與對邊軍的不信任。最內層是地方軍隊的實際利益：亞美尼亞軍區與安納托利亞邊軍長期負責對保加爾與薩爾馬提亞前線的警戒，軍功與掠奪物歸於自己，卻被要求服從首都的稅賦與調度。780年冬，亞美尼亞軍區的兵變趁皇帝本人身在安納托利亞而爆發，並迅速得到保加爾可汗的接應，把一場軍區抗命變成了對伊蓮王朝的正統挑戰。真正把雙方綁在一起的是共同語言：叛軍以恢復聖像為口號號召人心，朝廷則以保衛帝國正統回應。
causeEn: There are three layers to the reasons for the fighting. The outermost is religious: from the 730s the imperial government, with Constantine V at its centre, enforced iconoclasm, which alienated the western frontier soldiers and great numbers of the clergy; under Irene's regency the court tightened its control of the army, and the conflict could be lit at any moment. The middle layer is the succession: in 779 Leo IV died of illness, the six-year-old Constantine VI was poisoned by Irene's attendant, and in the years that followed the court repeatedly changed regents and churchmen, with episodes such as Arabaphus, Mokosios of Ephesus and the blinding of Nikephoros; to a theme strategos what this showed was palace intrigue in the capital and the distrust of the frontier. The innermost layer is the material interest of the local soldiers: the Armenian and Anatolic frontier forces had long guarded the line against the Bulgars and the Saracen frontier, won their glory and their plunder for themselves, and yet were ordered to obey the capital's taxes and dispatches. In the winter of 780 the mutiny of the Armenian theme broke out while the emperor himself was in Anatolia, and the Bulgar khagan joined in quickly, turning a military mutiny into a challenge to Irene's dynasty on the ground of legitimacy. What really bound the two sides together was a common language: the rebels called men with the cry of restoring the icons, and the court answered with the defence of imperial orthodoxy.
impact: 這場戰役的直接後果，是拜占庭重新拿回安納托利亞的軍區控制權：亞美尼亞軍區重新歸順，道路與驛站恢復，781年冬到783年的圍城期間，帝國得以從東方運兵、運糧而不受阻。這一點直接決定了接下來幾年的走向：帝國把注意力轉回西西里，782至785年組織了收復被薩拉森人佔領的北非與西西里的遠征，最終失敗，喪失了突尼斯的立足點，但出兵本身說明安納托利亞的內亂已經結束。更深一層的影響在宗教政治：叛軍的失敗削弱了軍隊中的聖像派力量，使787年第二次尼西亞會議得以召開，會議裁定聖像崇拜為正統，君士坦丁五世與教會達成某種和解，帝國換來了二十餘年的宗教平靜，直到815年第二次聖像破壞運動再起。而這場戰役也沒有解決根本問題：它證明邊軍、蠻族聯軍與宗教口號三者結合，就足以把帝國拖入內戰；伊蓮的王朝在797年被廢，同一批被鎮壓的派系在更小的規模上重現。對後世的軍事史而言，這是一個反覆出現的樣本：安納托利亞的縱深、堡壘與糧秣，比任何一次會戰的勝負更能決定拜占庭內戰的終局。
impactEn: The direct consequence of the battle was that Byzantium took back control of the Anatolic theme: the Armenian theme submitted again, the roads and relay stations were restored, and between the winter of 781 and 783 the empire could move troops and provisions eastwards without obstruction. That fact shaped the following years: the empire turned its attention back to Sicily, and between 782 and 785 it organised an expedition to recover the North African and Sicilian coastlines held by the Saracens; the expedition failed and the empire lost its foothold in Tunisia, but the fact that it could be launched at all shows that the Anatolian civil war was over. The deeper effect lay in religious politics: the defeat of the rebels weakened the iconoclast element within the army and made possible the Second Council of Nicaea of 787, which ruled that the veneration of icons was orthodox and sealed a kind of reconciliation between Constantine V and the church, buying the empire more than twenty years of religious peace until the second iconoclasm began in 815. Yet the battle settled nothing fundamental: it proved that frontier troops, barbarian allies and a religious slogan combined could drag the empire into civil war, and Irene's dynasty fell in 797, with the same suppressed factions resurfacing on a smaller scale. For later military history this is a recurring pattern, since the depth of Anatolia, its fortresses and its provisions decided the outcome of Byzantine civil wars more surely than the result of any single battle.
result: 結論是帝國的徹底勝利。保加爾可汗泰利斯在埃爾皮迪烏斯陣亡，被叛軍吸收的保加爾騎兵大部分散回保加爾方向，亞美尼亞與安納托利亞的叛軍被分割殲滅；被圍在安克拉的守軍在781年冬至783年的饑餓中出降，首領尼基福羅斯隨後被囚禁、刺瞎雙眼、剃髮送入聖狄奧多西修道院，追隨者則被分遣到色雷斯等地安置。皇帝君士坦丁五世因此贏得Kophas（瞽者）的綽號，這是他生前最後一次大規模野戰，此後他在775年去世，帝國隨即再度陷入攝政、幼主被毒與宮廷鬥爭的循環，797年伊蓮被廢，802年尼基福羅斯一世登基，帝國才回到君士坦丁王朝的秩序。整場內戰從780年起，到783年平定，前後約四年，動員範圍遍及安納托利亞、色雷斯與首都的禁軍，最終以叛軍全線瓦解、帝國軍制與教會重新綁定收場。留下的教訓極為實際：在一個以邊軍為骨幹的帝國裡，內戰的第一階段往往不是戰役，而是軍區的倒戈；決定勝負的是誰先控制道路、誰能把援軍送進堡壘、誰能在平原上讓敵人無法撤退。
resultEn: The outcome was a complete imperial victory. The Bulgar khagan Telis was killed at Elpidius, most of the Bulgar cavalry drawn into the revolt scattered back toward Bulgaria, and the rebel forces of Armenia and Anatolia were cut up and destroyed; the garrison besieged in Ancyra surrendered amid hunger between the winter of 781 and 783, and the leader Nikephoros was afterwards imprisoned, blinded in both eyes, tonsured and sent to the monastery of St Theodore, while his followers were dispersed and settled in Thrace and elsewhere. The emperor Constantine V gained the nickname Kophas, the Blinder; this was the last large field campaign of his life, and he died in 775, after which the empire fell back into the cycle of regency, the poisoning of young emperors and court intrigue, until Irene was deposed in 797 and Nikephoros I took the throne in 802, restoring the order of the Constantinian dynasty. The civil war as a whole lasted some four years, from 780 to its settlement in 783, and drew in Anatolia, Thrace and the garrison of the capital; it ended with the rebel cause broken across the board and the imperial military and the church tied together again. The lesson it leaves is very practical: in an empire built on frontier soldiers, the first stage of a civil war is usually not a battle but the defection of a theme, and what decides the outcome is who controls the roads first, who can bring reinforcements into the besieged fortress, and who can deny the enemy a place to retreat to on the open plain.
